We’re always excited to hear from people who are passionate about building a world where anyone, anywhere can thrive at work. If you don’t see a role that’s the right fit today, join our Talent Community to be considered for future opportunities.

By joining, you’ll:

- Be first to hear about new roles across Product, Engineering, Design, Sales, Marketing, Operations, People, and more

- Get insights into life at Oyster, our culture, and our mission

- Stay connected with our team for roles that match your skills and interests

WHAT WE LOOK FOR

- Curiosity, ownership, and a bias for action

- Strong communication and collaboration in distributed teams

- Commitment to inclusion, equity, and creating opportunity across borders

- Experience in one or more areas:

- Product and Engineering

- Design and Research

- Go‑to‑Market: Sales, Marketing, Customer Success

- Operations and Analytics

- People and Talent

- Finance and Legal

- EOR, payroll, HR technology, benefits, compliance, fintech, healthcare, logistics, or another regulated and operationally complex domain. Transferable experience counts where the complexity is comparable (multi-country rules, compliance exposure, human-in-the-loop workflows).

- Scaling products or workflows across countries, customers, teams, or markets.

Joining as a Business Development Representative (BDR) is your chance to take your outbound experience to the next level and build a long-term career in tech sales. Why you’ll love it here

You won’t be on your own. You’ll be surrounded by Business Development leaders, experienced Sales Executives, Revenue Operations experts, and an Enablement team that will help you ramp fast, sharpen your pitch, and keep improving every week. You’ll learn from people who’ve done the job and want to see you win.

AI-forward, and you own your process. Oyster is an AI-forward company, and our BDRs have real freedom to shape how they work. You’ll use the Nooks AI assistant (powered by Claude) and are encouraged to find your own ways to use AI to cut the busywork, so more of your day goes into real conversations with buyers.

Growth you earn. We take career progression seriously. Consistently hit your targets and you’ll earn protected time to build toward your next role, with coaching from BD leadership and our Enablement team. Your results open doors here, and we’ll help you walk through them.

Real impact from day one. You’ll be talking to HR, Finance, and Legal leaders at companies hiring across the world, helping them solve a problem that matters to their business. Every conversation you start feeds directly into how Oyster grows.

- Generate pipeline through high-volume, multichannel outbound: cold calls, email, and LinkedIn

- Research and map target accounts with multiple stakeholders, then build tailored outreach to senior leaders up to the C-suite

- Qualify prospects and book high-value meetings that convert into real opportunities for your Sales Executive partners

- Clearly articulate how Oyster’s global employment platform solves the problems your buyers face

- Run your book like a business: manage your pipeline, know your numbers, and keep finding smarter ways to work, including with AI

- Be the voice of the market, sharing buyer insight back to Sales, Marketing, and Product

- 6+ months as an SDR/BDR in B2B SaaS, with outbound prospecting as the core of your role (not primarily inbound)

- A track record of meeting or exceeding quota (meetings, SQLs, or SAOs), and you can walk us through your numbers

- Comfort with high-volume outreach across cold calling, email, and LinkedIn, and confidence on live calls with senior leaders

- Experience prospecting into accounts with multiple stakeholders, including the C-suite

- Hands-on experience with Salesforce and at least one sales engagement platform or dialer (e.g. Salesloft, Outreach, Nooks)

- A genuine interest in remote work and the trends shaping the global workplace

- Driven by a clear “why”: You’re motivated by more than money, whether it’s purpose, product, or your own growth, and it shows in how you show up every day.

- An owner: You take initiative, own your pipeline and your results, learn from mistakes, and find solutions instead of waiting for them.

- Always improving: You actively ask for feedback and put it into practice quickly. Here, that pays off: our Enablement team and BD leaders invest real time in coaching you.

- Resilient and persistent: You push through rejection, adapt your approach when something isn’t working, and keep the pipeline moving, and you’ll be surrounded by a team that does the same.

- A curious researcher: You dig into accounts, connect information from different sources, and use it to make your outreach sharper and more relevant.

- A team player with high standards: You lift your teammates up, celebrate team wins, and still hold yourself to a high bar on accuracy, organization, and results.

Your job is to turn that complexity into reliable, automated workflows.

You'll identify what's slowing teams down, question whether certain steps are needed at all, and build solutions that turn messy information into accurate, validated, payroll-ready data.

This is a hands-on role where you'll take ownership of defined automation projects, from understanding the problem and building a solution to launching it, monitoring performance, and making improvements.

You'll work with tools like n8n, Alteryx, SQL, APIs, and AI, but you won't be expected to use AI for everything. Sometimes the smartest solution is a simple rule, a better process, or preventing an issue before it happens.

- Fix the process, not just the task. Question unnecessary steps and look for ways to prevent missing information, avoidable requests, and errors before they reach payroll.

- Turn expert knowledge into reliable rules. Work with payroll and operations specialists to translate complex policies and requirements into clear, documented, version-controlled logic, including effective dates and required data.

- Put AI to practical use. Use large language models (LLMs) to understand requests, extract information from documents and emails, and direct cases to the right place. Build validation checks so AI-generated outputs are verified before they affect payroll.

- Build automations that actually run. Create, connect, and maintain workflows using n8n, Alteryx, and LLM-based tools, integrating service platforms, payroll systems, databases, APIs, and internal tools.

- Know when not to automate with AI. Choose between rule-based logic, workflow automation, AI, and human review depending on the task. Keep predictable legal and policy requirements in transparent, auditable rules, and document your decisions.

- Build reliability into every workflow. Include audit trails, error handling, alerts, exception queues, and appropriate approval controls. Make sure records are never silently changed, dropped, or excluded.

- Test before it matters. Build prototypes quickly, then test them against real payroll scenarios, unusual cases, and exceptions. Use shadow testing and parallel runs before introducing changes that affect live payroll.

- Make payroll operations more proactive. Automate timely information sharing, payroll-input checks, the identification of exceptions that affect pay, and reconciliation between payroll and invoices.

- Own what happens after launch. Track performance, measure whether automations deliver the expected improvements, troubleshoot issues, and improve or retire solutions that aren't working.

- Handle sensitive information responsibly. Apply privacy, security, and responsible-AI standards, especially when working with health, leave, or other sensitive payroll information. Make sure uncertain or compliance-sensitive cases reach the right people for review.

You'll likely enjoy this role if you like getting into the details of how things work, spotting opportunities others miss, and building solutions yourself.

- 3+ years of relevant experience in operations automation, process improvement, business or process analysis, payroll operations, internal tooling, or a similar field.

- You've built automations yourself. You've taken workflows into production using tools such as n8n, Alteryx, Make, Zapier, Power Automate, or similar, and have experience keeping them running. We're looking for someone who builds, not just someone who designs or documents solutions.

- You've used LLMs to solve practical problems. You know how to turn unstructured text or documents into usable data and can recognise when a simpler, rule-based solution is the better choice.

- You're comfortable connecting systems. You've worked with APIs, webhooks, and integrations to get different tools and data sources working together.

- You know your way around SQL and data. You can investigate, combine, validate, and analyse information from multiple sources, even when the underlying data is complex.

- You can bring structure to messy processes. You're able to turn inconsistent inputs, unusual cases, and complicated requirements into clear rules and data requirements.

- You take accuracy seriously. You understand the importance of checks, controls, and investigating discrepancies, particularly when errors could affect someone's pay.

- You can explain technical ideas clearly. You're comfortable working with non-technical colleagues, asking the right questions, and constructively challenging requests when automation isn't the best answer.

- You take ownership beyond the build. You can move from identifying a problem through implementation, testing, launch, monitoring, and ongoing maintenance.
